mainTopic: A widow whose husband died overseas: the doubt of a child from her צרה or a new son from her חמות, and whether we follow רוב or worry about a מיעוט.
overview: The משנה discusses a woman whose husband and צרה went to מדינת הים, and she then hears that her husband died. She may not marry anyone else, and she may not do יבום, until she knows whether her צרה had a child. The משנה adds that an ordinary חמות overseas is no worry. If the חמות left pregnant, she must worry that a new יבם was born, but רבי יהושע disagrees. The גמרא learns from the word היא that we worry only about the known צרה, not some unknown wife. It then asks why she cannot marry an outsider, since most women give birth. After testing whether the רבנן ignore a רוב דליתיה קמן, it proves from the ברייתא about minors and יבום that they do not, so the משנה must follow רבי מאיר, who worries about a מיעוט. The סיפא about the חמות seems to contradict רבי מאיר. The גמרא answers with her חזקה of being free to marry, and then with רב נחמן's distinction between כרת and לאו. רבא rejects that distinction, and his own answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Husband and co-wife go overseas, and news of his death arrives
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a woman told her husband died overseas may neither marry nor do יבום until she knows whether her צרה is pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman's husband and her co-wife traveled overseas. People came and told her, 'Your husband died.' She may not marry anyone else, and she may not do יבום, until she finds out whether her co-wife is pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents a case of doubt. Does this widow need יבום or not? It depends on whether her husband left a child through her צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband left a child, there is no יבום, and she may marry anyone. If he left no child, she is tied to the יבם and may not marry anyone else. Because we don't know which is true, both options are frozen for now.

keyTerms.meaning: co-wife (another wife of the same husband)

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole sugya is built on this double doubt. A child born to the husband cancels יבום, and having no child forbids marrying an outsider.

phrases.english: A woman whose husband and her co-wife went
to a country overseas,
and they came and told her: "Your husband died"
she may not marry, and she may not do יבום
until she knows
whether she, her co-wife, is pregnant.
phrases.notes: Notice the extra word 'she' (הִיא). The גמרא is going to ask why it is there.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ וְצָרָתָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Until the co-wife's pregnancy status is known, the widow may neither marry an outsider nor do יבום.

steps.title: A mother-in-law overseas, and one who left pregnant
steps.stepSummary: An ordinary חמות overseas causes no worry. A חמות who left pregnant does create a worry that a new brother-in-law was born.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she had a mother-in-law overseas, she does not need to worry. If the mother-in-law left while pregnant, she does need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a second kind of doubt: maybe her husband now has a brother who would require יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular חמות is not presumed to have a new son, so the widow may ignore her. But if the חמות left already pregnant, a brother may have been born. That brother would tie the widow to יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: she must be concerned / take the doubt into account

phrases.english: If she had a mother-in-law
phrases.notes: The case is one where her husband had no brothers, so a new baby boy would be the only possible יבם.

phrases.english: she need not be concerned.
If she left pregnant
she must be concerned.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary mother-in-law raises no concern. A mother-in-law who left pregnant does raise a concern of a new יבם.

steps.title: רבי יהושע says there is no concern
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues that even when the חמות left pregnant, the widow need not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: she does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע disagrees with the previous ruling about the pregnant חמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion worries about a brother who may have been born. רבי יהושע does not take this possible new brother into account, so the widow may marry freely.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two doubts. A pregnant צרה might cancel יבום. A pregnant חמות might create a new יבם, and on this one רבי יהושע says not to worry.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: she need not be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the ruling about the pregnant mother-in-law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if the mother-in-law left pregnant, the widow need not be concerned.

steps.title: Why does the משנה add the word 'she'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we learn from the words היא צרתה ('she, her co-wife').
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she, her co-wife' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking about the wording of the משנה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have simply said 'until she knows whether her co-wife is pregnant.' The extra word היא looks unnecessary, so the גמרא asks what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmudic discussion on the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is meant by "she, her co-wife"?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word היא in the משנה teaches

steps.title: We worry only about this co-wife, not an unknown one
steps.stepSummary: The word היא limits the worry to the specific צרה who traveled with him, not to some other wife he might have married overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: we worry only about this co-wife. We do not worry about some other co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The word 'she' narrows the concern to the known co-wife who went with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think we should also worry that the husband married a new wife overseas and had a child with her. The extra word tells us this is not a concern. Only the co-wife we know about, who actually went with him, causes doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it teaches us

phrases.english: It teaches us this:
it is about this co-wife that we are concerned,
but about another co-wife we are not concerned.
phrases.notes: He means a wife the husband might have married while he was overseas.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word היא limits the concern to the known co-wife who traveled with him. We ignore a possible new wife overseas.

steps.title: Why can't she marry someone else? Most women give birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the ban on יבום but challenges the ban on marrying an outsider. רוב says most women become pregnant and give birth, so the co-wife probably had a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'She may not marry and may not do יבום.' It makes sense that she may not do יבום, because maybe the co-wife is pregnant, and then she would be breaking the Torah ban of a brother's wife. But why may she not marry someone else? Follow the majority of women, and most women become pregnant and give birth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling and then challenges half of it. Not doing יבום is understood, but forbidding marriage to an outsider seems too strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the co-wife had a child, יבום would be a Torah ban of אשת אח, so we must be careful there. But we normally follow רוב, and most women do conceive and give birth. That suggests the husband likely left a child, which would free her to marry anyone. Step 7 suggests an answer, and step 13 settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: a brother's wife, forbidden by the Torah unless it is a מצוה of יבום
majority; we follow the usual case

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether she can do יבום. Everyone agrees she may not, since that risks a Torah ban. The challenge is only about marrying a different man.

phrases.english: "She may not marry and may not do יבום," etc.
Granted, she may not do יבום,
because perhaps she (the co-wife) is pregnant,
and she would run into the Torah ban of a brother's wife.
But that she may not marry, why?
Follow the majority of women,
and most women become pregnant and give birth!
phrases.notes: So the co-wife probably had a child, and that would free the widow to marry anyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's ruling to challenge its strictness
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that she may not marry another man
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Based on רוב, most women conceive and give birth, so we should assume a child was born. That would cancel יבום and allow her to marry anyone.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's worry follows רבי מאיר, who takes the minority into account.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to explain step 6's problem. Maybe the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who worries even about the small group of women who never give birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said that most women give birth, so the co-wife probably had a child. If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, that רוב is not enough, because he worries about the מיעוט. That explains why the widow may not marry an outsider.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)

phrases.english: Shall we say it is רבי מאיר
who is concerned about the minority?
phrases.notes: Here the minority means the few women who never become pregnant and give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests whose view the משנה follows, as a way to answer the רוב challenge of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה follow רבי מאיר, which would explain why it ignores the רוב of women who give birth?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the משנה follows a תנא (רבי מאיר) who does not rely on a רוב against a מיעוט
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since most women give birth, we should follow the רוב and let the widow marry an outsider.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who worries about the מיעוט of women who do not give birth, the ban on marrying an outsider makes sense. Step 8 challenges whether this is necessary, and step 13 finally accepts it.

steps.title: Even the רבנן only follow a majority that is in front of us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even the רבנן could agree here, because they only follow a רוב that is present, not a general statistic.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is the רבנן. When the רבנן follow the majority, it is a majority that is in front of us, like nine stores and the סנהדרין. But a majority that is not in front of us, the רבנן do not follow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says we do not need to say the משנה is only רבי מאיר. It splits a רוב into two kinds and says the רבנן only rely on the first kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רוב דאיתיה קמן is a real group you can count, like nine kosher stores against one non-kosher store, or the judges of the סנהדרין voting. A רוב דליתיה קמן is a general fact about how the world usually works, like 'most women give birth.' The claim is that the רבנן do not rely on that second kind, so even they would worry in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A majority that is in front of us (you can count it)
A majority that is not in front of us (a general pattern)
Nine stores: the classic case of meat found near nine kosher stores and one non-kosher store
The סנהדרין, which decides by majority vote

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן never follow a רוב. The claim here is only that they follow a רוב you can actually see and count, not a general 'most people are like this' רוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between a counted רוב and a general-pattern רוב is a well-known distinction that comes up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis;
when the Rabbis go after the majority,
it is a majority that is in front of us,
for example, nine stores and the Sanhedrin.
But a majority that is not in front of us,
the Rabbis do not go after the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Avoids the need to say the משנה is only רבי מאיר by limiting when the רבנן follow a רוב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the משנה must be רבי מאיר; it says the רבנן could agree too.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 7 assumed the רבנן would follow any רוב, but they only follow a רוב that is present and can be counted.

steps.title: But the רבנן follow a hidden majority with a minor boy and girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 8: in the case of a קטן and קטנה, the רבנן rely on a רוב that is not in front of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at a minor boy and minor girl: that is a majority not in front of us, and still the רבנן follow the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea from step 8. It points to a case where the רבנן do rely on a general-pattern רוב, and it will prove this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the רבנן never rely on a רוב דליתיה קמן. Whether a child will grow up able to have children is exactly that kind of general pattern. If the רבנן rely on it there, step 8's distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor boy and a minor girl

phrases.english: But there is the case of a minor boy and minor girl,
which is a majority that is not in front of us,
and the Rabbis do go after the majority!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה דְּרוּבָּא דְּלֵיתָא קַמַּן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that the רבנן do not follow a רוב דליתיה קמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a known case, minors and יבום, where the רבנן rely on a general-pattern רוב, so they do follow that kind of רוב.

steps.title: The ברייתא: minors and חליצה and יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר forbids minors from both חליצה and יבום, and the רבנן agree only about חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: a minor boy and minor girl do not do חליצה and do not do יבום, says רבי מאיר. They said to him: you are right that they do not do חליצה, because 'man' is written in that section, and we compare a woman to a man. But why can they not do יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its challenge. In the ברייתא, the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר about חליצה and then ask him why he also forbids יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חליצה there is a verse, 'איש,' that requires an adult man. Since the woman is compared to the man, she must be an adult too. For יבום there is no such verse, so the רבנן want to know רבי מאיר's reason for forbidding it.

keyTerms.meaning: We compare (one thing to another, based on the verse)

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה לֹא חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין,
phrases.english: A minor boy and minor girl do not do חליצה and do not do יבום;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
They said to Rabbi Meir:
You said well that they do not do חליצה.
'Man' is written in the section,
and we compare the woman to the man.
But what is the reason they do not do יבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא קָטָן וּקְטַנָּה לֹא חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that backs up the challenge of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the רבנן follow a רוב דליתיה קמן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about minors doing חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason: the child might turn out unable to have children
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that the boy may turn out to be a סריס and the girl an איילונית, and then the יבום would be a forbidden relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: the minor boy might turn out to be a סריס, the minor girl might turn out to be an איילונית, and then they would end up with a forbidden relationship.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי מאיר answers the רבנן's question. He forbids יבום for minors because of the small chance that they cannot have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום only applies when it is possible to have children. If the child turns out to be a סריס or an איילונית, there was never a מצוה of יבום, and the woman stays forbidden as a brother's wife, an ערוה. רבי מאיר worries about this small minority.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who is physically unable to have children
A woman who is physically unable to have children
A forbidden relationship (here, a brother's wife)

phrases.english: He said to them:
A minor boy, lest he turn out to be a סריס;
a minor girl, lest she turn out to be an איילונית;
and they would end up running into a forbidden relationship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם קָטָן שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא סָרִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question the רבנן asked רבי מאיר inside the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר forbids יבום for minors because the minority who turn out to be a סריס or an איילונית would make the act a forbidden relationship.

steps.title: The רבנן follow the majority of children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the רבנן rely on the רוב: most children do not turn out to be a סריס or an איילונית. That is a רוב that is not in front of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: follow the majority of minor boys, and most minor boys are not סריסים. Follow the majority of minor girls, and most minor girls are not איילוניות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. The רבנן allow minors to do יבום because they rely on the רוב of children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Most children grow up able to have children' is a general pattern, a רוב דליתיה קמן. The רבנן rely on it anyway. This shows that step 8 was wrong: the רבנן do follow this kind of רוב.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
Go after the majority of minor boys,
and most minor boys are not סריסים.
Go after the majority of minor girls,
and most minor girls are not איילוניות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי זִיל בָּתַר רוּבָּא דִּקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning of the רבנן, which completes the proof against step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן follow a רוב דליתיה קמן, which undoes the distinction of step 8.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reasoning of the רבנן in the ברייתא, who rely on the majority of minors.

steps.title: It is clear: the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן would follow even a hidden רוב, the משנה's worry must follow רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that our משנה is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the attempt to fit the משנה with the רבנן. It goes back to the suggestion from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן would rely on 'most women give birth' and let the widow marry an outsider. The משנה does not allow this, so it must follow רבי מאיר, who worries about the מיעוט. This answers the challenge from step 6.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's worry that the co-wife might not have had a child follows רבי מאיר, who worries about the מיעוט. The רבנן follow even a רוב that is not in front of us, as we see with minors and יבום.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
that our mishna is Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the distinction of step 8 has been disproven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who worries about the מיעוט of women who do not give birth. That is why the widow may not marry an outsider.

steps.title: The mother-in-law case seems to contradict רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who worries about a מיעוט, then in the סיפא she should worry that her mother-in-law gave birth to a boy, since boys are a מיעוט of all pregnancies.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said the משנה follows רבי מאיר. But look at the end: if she has a mother-in-law, she does not worry. Why not? Most women get pregnant and give birth, a few miscarry, and half of the births are girls. Add the miscarriages to the girls, and boys are only a minority. רבי מאיר worries about a minority, so she should worry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 13 by pointing to the סיפא of the משנה, which does not seem to fit רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mother-in-law overseas could give birth to a new son, who would be a brother of the dead husband and so a יבם. Boys come out to be only a מיעוט of pregnancies once you add miscarriages to the girls. Since רבי מאיר worries about a מיעוט, the משנה should tell her to worry, yet it says she does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה

phrases.english: In what way did you establish it? According to Rabbi Meir.
Say the latter clause:
If she had a mother-in-law, she need not be concerned.
phrases.notes: The worry would be that the mother-in-law gave birth to a new son, who would be a brother-in-law needing יבום.

phrases.english: Why?
Follow the majority of women,
and most women become pregnant and give birth,
a minority miscarry,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַיּוֹלְדוֹת — מֶחֱצָה זְכָרִים וּמֶחֱצָה נְקֵבוֹת.
phrases.english: and of all who give birth, half are males and half are females.
Join the minority who miscarry to the half who have females,
and then the males become the minority,
so let him be concerned!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 13 that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר worries about a מיעוט; a newborn boy is a מיעוט; yet the סיפא says she need not worry, which does not fit רבי מאיר.

steps.title: She is presumed free to marry anyone
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps רבי מאיר does not worry here because the woman already has a חזקה that she may marry anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe since she is presumed free to marry anyone, he does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the idea that the משנה follows רבי מאיר by pointing to the woman's current legal status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When her husband died, he had no known brothers, so she has a חזקה of being free to marry any man. A חזקה is strong enough that even רבי מאיר does not worry about a מיעוט against it.

keyTerms.meaning: She was established with a legal presumption (חזקה)
To the market, meaning free to marry anyone

phrases.english: Perhaps, since she is presumed free to marry the public,
he is not concerned.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing factor: a חזקה outweighs the worry about a מיעוט
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר should worry about any מיעוט, including a newborn brother-in-law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the woman has a חזקה of being free to marry, רבי מאיר does not worry about the מיעוט.

steps.title: Then in the רישא she should do יבום
steps.stepSummary: If a חזקה beats the worry, then in the רישא, where she is presumed ready for יבום, she should be allowed to do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first clause, she is presumed ready for יבום, so let her do יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer of step 15 against the רישא of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא her husband left no known children, so she has a חזקה of needing יבום. If a חזקה beats a מיעוט, she should not worry that her rival wife gave birth, yet the משנה says she does worry.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
Let her be taken in levirate marriage

phrases.english: In the first clause, where she is presumed to require levirate marriage,
let her enter into levirate marriage!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a חזקה removes the worry
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא also has a חזקה (for יבום), yet the משנה still worries there; so the חזקה cannot be the reason.

steps.title: A כרת prohibition is more serious than a לאו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: in the רישא the risk is a כרת sin, so they worried; in the סיפא the risk is only a לאו, so they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The first clause involves a כרת prohibition, so they were concerned. The latter clause involves a regular לאו, so they were not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 16 by saying the two halves of the משנה differ in how serious the possible sin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, if the rival wife had a living child, there is no יבום and marrying the brother is אשת אח, which carries כרת. In the סיפא, if a brother was born, marrying someone else without חליצה is only a לאו. So the חזקה is relied upon only for the lighter sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The first clause, which involves a prohibition of karet, they were concerned;
phrases.notes: If the rival wife had a child, the brother's wife is forbidden to him, which is a כרת sin.

phrases.english: the latter clause, which involves an ordinary prohibition, they were not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ רֵישָׁא דְּאִיסּוּר כָּרֵת חָשְׁשׁוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction by severity of the possible sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חזקה should work the same way in both clauses.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a כרת prohibition they worried even against a חזקה; for a לאו they relied on the חזקה.

steps.title: רבא: both are Torah prohibitions, so there is no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the split between כרת and לאו, since both are Torah laws, and begins to give his own answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both of these are Torah laws, so what difference does it make whether it is a כרת prohibition or a regular לאו? Rather, רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the answer of step 17, and then sets up his own new answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argues that the strength of a doubt does not change just because one sin is harsher, as long as both are Torah law. So the כרת versus לאו split cannot explain why one clause worries and the other does not. The words "אלא אמר רבא" open a new explanation that continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it to me

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two clauses still need an explanation: רבא rejected the כרת and לאו split and is about to offer his own answer.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now since this is by Torah law and that is by Torah law,
what difference is it to me if it is a prohibition of karet
or what difference is it to me if it is an ordinary prohibition?!
Rather, Rava said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא מִכְּדֵי הָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא וְהָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 and opens a new answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole distinction of רב נחמן between כרת and לאו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both prohibitions are Torah law, so the level of punishment should not change how we treat the doubt.
